title: The Night Ice
hook: The old rink manager had one rule: after the last flood of the ice, if you hear skating in the dark... don't turn the lights back on.
lines: The old rink manager gave me one rule for the night shift.
After the last flood of the ice, if you hear skating in the dark... don't turn the lights back on.
For six weeks, I laid down fresh ice, killed the lights, and locked up. Nothing ever happened.
Then, one night in December, I was halfway to the exit when I heard it.
Scrape... scrape... scrape. Long, slow strokes, circling the rink.
I froze. My hand was already on the light switch.
And a small voice, right against the glass, whispered... Can you turn the lights on? I can't find the door.
I didn't. I ran... and I left the back door swinging open behind me.
In the morning, my perfect ice had one set of tiny skate marks on it.
They circled the rink for hours... then went straight through the gate, down the hall, and out that open door.
This morning, there were long, thin scratches on my kitchen floor... going around, and around, and around.
